name: Anthracene extraction and oxidation
note: Anthracene is the highest boiling component of coal tar. It crystallises readily and is extremely pure after recrystallisation. name: Coal tar fractionation and distillation
note: Coal tar boiling below 300 C contains benzene, toluene, phenol. Above 300 C come naphthalene and anthracene. Fractional distillation with bubble-cap trays gives cuts of surprising purity if reflux is high. The vapour pressure differences are only a factor of two, so reflux ratio must exceed 10:1 to separate them properly.

name: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) synthesis
note: Vinyl chloride is made by acetylene plus HCl or ethylene dichloride cracking. Polymerisation in aqueous emulsion yields PVC plastic. Plasticisers are added to make flexible sheet; unplasticised PVC is rigid and chemical-resistant. PVC is the most widely used plastic on Earth. Thermal decomposition releases hydrogen chloride, making fires extremely dangerous.

name: Toluene extraction from coal tar
note: Toluene boils at 111 C, well separated from benzene at 80 C. A fractionating column yields toluene at 99% purity. Toluene is used as a solvent and as a precursor to TNT and saccharin. It is less toxic than benzene but still a CNS depressant at high vapour concentrations.

name: Caisson and underwater excavation
note: A large hollow box sunk into water or soft ground, interior pumped dry, filled with concrete. London Bridge (1831) used caissons. Allows foundation work below water. name: Dredging for channel maintenance
note: Sediment fills harbours and channels; dredges scoop it up. Early dredges were buckets on a chain driven by water power. Suction dredges (pump-driven) are later but far more powerful. Maintenance dredging is expensive and continuous. The removed material can be sold or used for land reclamation.

name: Pumping station and mechanical lift
note: A water-powered pump (or steam-powered later) lifts water uphill against gravity. The Archimedean screw predates Rome; centrifugal pumps came later. Lifting water to a tower gives pressure for distribution. Without lift, you must be lower than the source.

name: Water treatment works and coagulation
note: Alum added to water causes clay particles to coagulate and settle. Sand filters then remove fine particles and some bacteria. Boiling kills most pathogens. Chlorine (post-1900) kills the rest. Water treatment makes urban life possible; sewage in the water kills you fast.

name: Antenna and ground system for radio
note: An antenna is just a wire at a height or length that couples to the air (transmitting) or the air couples to it (receiving). A ground is a connection to earth (literally a copper plate or rod buried 2 metres). Radio waves need an antenna and a return path (ground) to form a closed loop. name: Telegraph power supply - voltaic cells in series
note: Telegraph stations need reliable, large current (amps, not milliamps). A Daniell cell or Grove cell in series provides 1-2 volts. A telegraph key and relay need about 1 amp at 10-100 volts. The maintenance burden is high: cells need refilling, electrodes corrode, acid must be managed safely. This cost and complexity drives later adoption of central powerhouses.

name: Triode oscillator - audio and RF frequency synthesis
note: A triode with feedback can generate any frequency from audio (10 Hz) to microwave (1000 MHz), tuned by the LC circuit. name: Fire-refined copper stock
note: Poling and fire refining to get copper clean enough to draw into long fine wire without breaking. A separate node from electro-refining because you need it before you have any electricity.

name: Destructive distillation of wood and coal
note: Wood gives methanol, acetic acid, tar and charcoal. Coal gives coke, coal gas, coal tar and ammonia liquor. Coal tar is the gateway to phenol, benzene, aniline dyes and eventually plastics; coal gas gives you street lighting, which is a spectacular and profitable public benefaction.

name: Electromagnet, relay, and the Wheatstone bridge
note: Iron amplifying a current's magnetism is the effect on which motors, generators, telegraphs and relays all rest. It is also the most alarming demonstration you will give: heavy iron moving at a distance with no visible cause.

name: Central heating by hot water radiator
note: Boiler in basement or furnace room heats water, which circulates through cast-iron radiators in all rooms. Replaces fireplaces and central stove heating. Enables uniform comfort; transforms house design. Requires piping, a circulating pump, and constant fuel supply.

name: Shampoo, soap-based
note: Soap solution with perfume. Romans wash hair with lye (harsh) or oil. Soap-based shampoo is gentle and effective. Liquid and powdered forms compete; bars arrive later. Fragrance matters for premium products.

name: Oxygen and hydrogen in quantity
note: Zinc or iron with acid gives hydrogen; heating manganese dioxide or a chlorate gives oxygen. Needed for the oxy-hydrogen torch, for fused quartz, for balloons, and later for reducing germanium oxide to metal. Hydrogen and air is an explosive mixture over a very wide range; be disciplined.

name: Boneshaker (pedal bicycle)
note: Pedals drive the front wheel directly via crank. Frame and wheels are wood and cast iron, hence the name. Rider feels every rock; suspension comes later. Speed gain over walking is 2x. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

name: Tin plate production
note: Electroplate iron sheet with tin or dip into molten tin. Tin is non-toxic and corrosion-resistant, so tinned steel is ideal for food storage. The tin coating must be continuous or rust starts at the pin-holes. Electroplated tin plate is thinner and cheaper than dipped; dipped is thicker but more durable. The difference is in the tin-iron bond strength.

name: True plane surfaces by the three-plate method
note: The foundation of everything mechanical, and it needs nothing Rome does not have. Two plates lapped together converge on a matched sphere and socket. Three plates lapped in rotation can only converge on flat. From the plane you derive the straightedge, the square, the gauge, the screw, and every machine after.

name: Loudspeaker
note: Coil in magnetic field vibrates diaphragm. Reverses microphone. Weak signal amplified for audible volume.

name: Stereotype plate
note: Plaster impression of type. Molten type poured into mould. Reusable, faster than resetting type.

name: Electric motor and end of line shafting
note: Individual electric motors at each machine, replacing the central steam engine and line shafting running through the factory. This is a larger productivity gain than any single machine: workers control their own pace, maintenance is local, floor space opens up.

name: Stirling engine
